title: Fluffernutter and the Sky-Puddle
markdown:
High on Snowberry Hill, where the air felt happy and quiet, lived a young goblin named Glim. And who could be a better friend than Fluffernutter, Glim's own fluffy lamb? Fluffernutter was white and woolly, like a little happy cloud with ears as soft as flower petals. His little pink nose wiggled with fun.

One sunny morning, sunbeams danced through the leaves like playful sprites. Glim’s bright eyes sparkled! He and Fluffernutter danced in the woods. The big green ferns tickled Glim’s knees. Glim hummed a happy goblin song. Fluffernutter trotted beside him. His soft feet made a quiet *tap-tap-tap* on the soft moss. The air smelled sweet and earthy.

Then, Fluffernutter stopped. His ears stood up straight! He wiggled with excitement. He saw something very special! "Baa?" he asked softly. He pointed his nose. Right there, by an old, big oak tree, was a puddle. Oh, how it sparkled! It looked just like the blue sky! White clouds floated in its middle. Fluffernutter thought it looked like a fun friend. He wanted to jump in!

Glim knelt beside his lamb. He put his green hand on Fluffernutter’s soft wool. "Oh, Fluffernutter," Glim whispered. His voice was like rustling leaves. "That’s not the sky, little one. It's water. It looks like the sky because it’s shiny and blue. But it’s too wet for jumping. It would make your wool soggy and cold. We don't want that!" A tiny worry, like a dewdrop, tickled Glim's nose. He needed to help his curious lamb.

A rumbling sound, like friendly thunder, made them look up. Here came Barnaby, the ogre cook! His big hands held a basket of juicy red snowberries. Barnaby’s laugh was a happy sound. His big eyes were warm like a fireplace.

"Hullo, Glim! Hullo, Fluffernutter!" Barnaby rumbled. "What's this puzzle?" He saw Fluffernutter staring at the sky-puddle.

"Barnaby," Glim said, his voice like a tiny fairy bell. "Fluffernutter thinks this puddle is the sky. He wants to play with the clouds."

Barnaby chuckled. "Ah, a sky-puddle! They do look like the sky, don’t they? Shiny reflections! But you know," he whispered to Glim, "sometimes, if you offer something else, something even more fun, a friend forgets the first thing." He winked his big eye.

Glim's goblin brain whirred. A different, fun thing! He looked at Fluffernutter, still staring at the puddle. Glim reached into his little goblin pouch. He pulled out a bright red snowberry! It was perfectly round and very juicy.

"Fluffernutter!" Glim chirped, holding up the berry. "Look! A sparkly red berry! It's much tastier than sky-water! A special treat for you!"

Fluffernutter's pink nose twitched. A berry! A shiny red one! His eyes left the puddle. He nudged Glim’s hand. He happily munched the sweet berry. *Munch, munch, munch.* He forgot all about the sky-puddle.

Glim smiled a big, happy smile. "See? All better! A yummy berry is more fun than a wet puddle," he whispered. Barnaby nodded. The woods felt safe and happy. The trees remember this story well. They whisper that a kind friend and a juicy berry can solve almost any sky-puddle problem. Who could have guessed it would be so simple and so delightful?
characters: Glim the young goblin, a lamb
